Subject: Pack portability & upgrade question for pilot

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency numbers. Before we sign the pilot SOW I want to confirm a couple of packaging details so our procurement and infra teams can sign off:

1) If we start on the Compact pack and later need to upgrade to Dedicated, what happens to the feature entitlements (live model variants, streaming, and priority routing)? Do entitlements port automatically or do we need to repurchase certain add-ons?

2) Are multi-environment keys (hosted + private) covered in the same pack or billed separately? Our security team is insisting on a private VPC for PII-bound flows while we keep non-PII traffic in hosted.

3) Any chance to align upgrade credits/discounts to avoid a big one-time sticker shock at the point of upgrade?

I attached our usage export for Q2 to give you an idea of the footprint. If it helps, we can schedule a short call with procurement.

Thanks,
Ami Rao
Head of Platform Engineering
CloudHarbor, Inc.
attachments: CloudHarbor_usage_2026Q2.csv

Subject: Re: Pack portability & upgrade question for pilot

Hi Ami — really appreciate the usage export, that makes this much easier. Quick answers up front, then a suggested path: 

- Entitlement portability: core entitlements (streaming, model variants support) are portable when you move between packs; certain Dedicated-only features (reserved GPU pools, per-tenant isolation, SLA credits) are dedicated add-ons and will be added on upgrade.

- Multi-environment keys: we can include hosted API keys and a private deployment license under the same commercial agreement. Billing is typically consolidated but with clear line-items for private infra usage.

- Upgrade credits: we offer a prorated credit against committed spend for upgrades completed within the first 12 months of the pilot, and we can outline a ladder of step discounts tied to committed throughput.

If you're flexible, I propose a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk procurement through the exact line items and to show a sample amendment. Ben, Priyom — can you join? I'm going to attach a pack-comparison PDF and a simple MAP (mutual-action-plan) template so procurement can see the timeline and credit mechanics.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Principal Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

Hi Ami — quick technical clarification to set expectations: 

1) When you convert from Compact to Dedicated we will preserve model weights, KV caches are per-deployment and won't be automatically migrated — we can help orchestrate a hot-swap with a short grace period, but large prefix caches may need a warmup window.

2) Streaming + model variants: identical APIs; the Dedicated environment will enable priority preemption and reserved throughput which means slightly different operational SLAs.

3) VPC/private wiring: our private deployment includes a single deployment license that can be replicated across a region; if you want both hosted and private simultaneously we recommend the dual-key approach Sofia mentioned (single PO, separate line-items).

If helpful, I can spin up a short architecture note for procurement that shows the migration steps and any expected downtime (very minimal) — say 15 minutes of throttling during cutover in most cases.

— Priyom
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
